operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of password reset issuance records that belong to the currently authenticated member account.

This operation exposes a read-oriented view over the password reset support data stored in the todo_app_member_password_resets table. Each record represents a reset issuance event associated with a specific todo_app_members record and includes the unique reset token, its expiration timestamp, whether it has been consumed through the used_at column, and the audit timestamps that indicate when the record was issued and last updated. The endpoint is intended for account-scoped inspection of reset activity rather than direct credential management.

Access to this operation is restricted to an authenticated member and must always be evaluated in the signed-in member's own account context. The application supports self-owned access boundaries, and account-management requirements state that a member can act only on their own account data. Therefore, this operation must never return password reset records that belong to another member, and it must not accept a member identifier from the client to widen or override the authenticated scope.

The response should be optimized for list browsing and include paginated summary entries rather than unrelated account profile data. Filtering and sorting should be based only on fields that actually exist in the password reset schema, such as token, expired_at, used_at, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. This allows clients to browse active reset issuances, previously consumed reset issuances, expired records, or historical issuance activity without assuming fields that are not defined in the database.

This operation is related to account recovery and password lifecycle workflows, but it does not itself change a member password and does not issue a new reset token. Password change behavior remains governed by the account-management requirements, where the signed-in member changes only their own password and a rejected change leaves the existing password unchanged. In contrast, this endpoint is purely for retrieval of reset-record information within the caller's own account boundary.

If no records match the supplied search criteria, the operation should return a valid empty paginated result rather than failing. If the caller is not authenticated, access must be rejected. If filtering inputs are malformed or unsupported, the request should be rejected according to validation rules derived from the request DTO. Sensitive handling is required because reset tokens are authentication artifacts, so implementations should carefully consider whether summaries mask or partially redact token values when shaping the response DTO.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement this operation as an authenticated collection query over todo_app_member_password_resets limited to the current member derived from the session or authentication context.

Resolve the signed-in member identifier first. If the request is unauthenticated, reject it before any database access. Do not accept or trust any client-supplied member identifier in the request body because ownership scope must come exclusively from the authenticated account context.

Build a database query against todo_app_member_password_resets with a mandatory predicate on todo_app_member_id = currentMemberId. Exclude rows only according to the semantics defined by ITodoAppMemberPasswordReset.IRequest; if the request supports historical browsing, deleted_at may be filterable rather than implicitly excluded. Apply optional filters only for actual schema fields, such as token matching, used_at nullability state, expired_at range, created_at range, updated_at range, and deleted_at presence. Do not reference undeclared fields.

Apply deterministic pagination and sorting. Default sorting should prioritize the most recently created reset records first using created_at descending unless the request DTO specifies another allowed sort based on real columns. Return a paginated envelope consistent with IPageITodoAppMemberPasswordReset.ISummary. Each summary item should be derived from the password reset record and should avoid exposing unnecessary member credential data from todo_app_members. If token exposure is considered sensitive in the DTO contract, return a masked or limited representation consistent with the schema definition used downstream.

The query can be implemented without a join when only reset-record fields are needed, because the ownership filter uses todo_app_member_id already stored on the table. A join to todo_app_members is optional only for authorization verification or future enrichment, but no member data outside the caller's own account may be exposed.

Handle edge cases explicitly: return an empty page when no records match; reject invalid pagination or unsupported sort options through request validation; and ensure expired and used-state filtering is computed from expired_at and used_at as stored values rather than inferred from non-existent status columns. Because this is a read operation, no transaction beyond the database read consistency provided by the ORM is generally required.

operations.description:
Retrieve one password reset record that belongs to the currently authenticated member account.

This operation returns the detailed state of a single password reset issuance record from the password reset support entity associated with a member account. The underlying database entity stores a one-time reset credential with expiration and consumption tracking, including the unique reset token, the time the record was issued, the time it expires, and whether it has already been consumed. In this private todo application, the password reset record is not a shared business object; it is an account-bound authentication support record linked to the owning member through the member relationship.

Access to this operation is restricted to the authenticated member who owns the referenced password reset record. The service must evaluate the request in the current signed-in account context and must not reveal whether another member owns the record. This aligns with the application's private ownership model, where account-related actions apply only to the current account holder and cross-user access is not permitted.

The returned resource reflects the lifecycle of the password reset issuance as stored in the database schema. The response may be used by clients that need to inspect whether a reset record exists for the current member, whether it has already been used, and whether it is still within its valid period according to the expired_at and used_at columns. Because the table also contains deletion tracking, implementations should treat logically removed records as unavailable unless the product explicitly requires them to remain visible.

This operation is related to password recovery and account management flows, but it does not perform a password change by itself. Password replacement is governed by the account management requirements that keep the same member account and private todo space intact after a successful password change. This endpoint only retrieves one reset record and does not create, modify, consume, or remove reset credentials.

If the caller is not authenticated, if the referenced record does not exist, or if the record does not belong to the current member account, the request must fail without exposing another member's account data. Clients should use this operation only when they already possess a password reset record identifier associated with the currently signed-in member context.

If no row matches, return a not-found style failure that does not disclose whether the identifier exists for another account. If a row is found, map the entity to the ITodoAppMemberPasswordReset response DTO using the actual schema fields from the table. Include the primary identifier, owning member linkage as permitted by the DTO contract, token value if the DTO exposes it, issuance timestamp, expiration timestamp, usage timestamp, update timestamp, and deletion timestamp only if the schema type includes it.

Do not mutate the record during retrieval. This operation must not mark a token as used, refresh expiration, or create any additional audit rows. It is a pure read operation.

Validate that the passwordResetId path parameter is a UUID before querying. operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of email verification records that belong to the signed-in member.

This operation provides a member-scoped view of the email verification artifacts stored in the underlying todo_app_member_email_verifications table. That table represents issued verification records that prove ownership of a member email address during registration or later verification flows, and each record tracks its lifecycle through the token value, expiration time, successful use time, optional revocation time, issuance time, and last update time. The endpoint is intended for structured browsing of a member's own verification record history and current verification states rather than direct management of verification tokens.

Access to this operation is limited to the authenticated member acting within their own private account context. The application defines only a single member actor, and that actor is not permitted to act for another user or browse another account's private information. For that reason, the operation must evaluate all reads within the signed-in member's own account boundary and must never disclose verification records that belong to a different member. The caller does not provide a member identifier in the path because the account scope is derived from authentication.

The response should be optimized for list browsing. Clients can submit pagination, filtering, and sorting criteria to narrow the result set by lifecycle state such as active, used, revoked, expired, or deleted-record visibility if such options are represented in the request DTO. The returned summaries should help the member understand when verification records were issued, whether they were consumed, whether they expired, and whether they were revoked, without requiring the caller to access unrelated account data.

This operation is related to registration and verification workflows but does not perform those workflows itself. Registration is the upstream process that can cause the system to issue verification artifacts, and successful verification or replacement flows can update used_at or revoked_at values. This endpoint only reads the resulting records. It should not be treated as an API for issuing tokens, consuming tokens, or editing stored verification state.

If the caller is not authenticated, the request must be rejected without revealing whether any member account exists. If the caller is authenticated, the system should return only that caller's records, and an empty page is valid when no matching verification records exist for the submitted criteria.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement this operation as a member-scoped search over the todo_app_member_email_verifications table.

Authenticate the caller as a member and resolve the signed-in member's primary identifier from the active session context. Build the query so that todo_app_member_id is always constrained to the authenticated member id. Do not accept or infer any alternate account scope from the request body, and do not expose records for any other member under any condition.

Parse the ITodoAppMemberEmailVerification.IRequest body as structured list criteria. Support pagination inputs defined in the request DTO and apply deterministic ordering. The default ordering should prioritize the most recently issued or updated verification records first, using created_at descending as the primary fallback if no explicit sort is provided. If the request DTO includes state filters, translate them from business intent into timestamp predicates against expired_at, used_at, revoked_at, and deleted_at. For example, used records are identified by non-null used_at, revoked records by non-null revoked_at, expired records by expired_at earlier than the current server time when not already used, and active records by a future expired_at with null used_at and null revoked_at. Only implement filters that are actually present in the DTO.

Select only the fields needed for the summary projection defined by ITodoAppMemberEmailVerification.ISummary and return them inside IPageITodoAppMemberEmailVerification.ISummary. Include pagination metadata required by the page DTO. If deleted-record visibility is not part of the request DTO, exclude rows with deleted_at set; if the DTO explicitly supports that visibility, apply the requested policy accordingly.

Do not mutate any verification record in this operation. Do not issue new tokens, consume tokens, revoke tokens, or update timestamps here. This endpoint is strictly for reading verification history and status. Return an empty paginated result when the authenticated member has no matching records. Reject unauthenticated access according to the application's authentication failure behavior without disclosing account existence or any private data.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single email verification record that belongs to the authenticated member account.

This operation returns detailed information about one email verification artifact stored for a member in the private todo application. The underlying resource is backed by the todo_app_member_email_verifications table, which is described as the record that proves ownership of a member email address during registration or later verification flows. The returned resource represents a single issued verification token and its lifecycle timestamps, including when it expires, whether it has been used successfully, whether it was revoked before use, and when the record was created or last updated.

Access to this operation is restricted to the authenticated member who owns the verification record. The todo_app_member_email_verifications row belongs to exactly one todo_app_members row through todo_app_member_id, and the application requirements state that authenticated access is limited to the member's own private account context only. Accordingly, this endpoint must never disclose another member's verification record, account details, profile information, or todo information. If the requester is not authenticated, access must be rejected. If the record does not belong to the authenticated member, the request must also be rejected.

From a data-model perspective, this operation exposes an authorization-supporting child resource rather than a user-managed business object. The email verification table stores the unique verification token and lifecycle columns expired_at, used_at, revoked_at, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. The parent member account stores the email sign-in identity and the email_verified flag that indicates whether email ownership has been verified for the account. This retrieval operation is useful for presenting verification status or audit-style details within the member's own account context, but it does not create, modify, consume, or remove verification records.

Clients should use this endpoint only after the member has been authenticated into their own account context. The operation is independent from sign-in itself and must not reveal whether any unrelated account exists. Expected failures include unauthenticated access, requests for a nonexistent verification record, and requests for a record owned by another member. In all such cases, the system should avoid exposing sensitive ownership or account-discovery details beyond the minimum necessary error response.

If authentication is missing or invalid, reject the request as unauthorized. If no verification record exists for the given id within the authenticated member's ownership scope, reject the request as not found or forbidden according to the service's standard ownership-safe error policy. Do not reveal whether the id exists under another member account.

Map the result to ITodoAppMemberEmailVerification, including the verification lifecycle fields and ownership-related reference fields defined by the DTO contract. Do not mutate token state in this operation: do not mark the verification as used, do not revoke it, and do not update member.email_verified. This endpoint is strictly read-only.

Ensure sensitive token-handling rules remain consistent with security expectations. The implementation may redact or omit highly sensitive token presentation details in downstream serialization if the DTO contract requires it, but it must remain faithful to the actual schema-driven response type. operations.description:
Retrieve the signed-in member's own private profile.

This operation returns the profile record that belongs to the currently authenticated member in the todoApp personal workspace. The underlying profile entity is intentionally minimal: according to the database schema for `todo_app_profiles`, it stores profile-specific identity data separately from authentication credentials in `todo_app_members`, and its primary business attribute is `display_name`, the private display name shown for the member inside the personal workspace. This endpoint is therefore the canonical read operation for presenting that private profile identity inside the member's own account context.

Access to this operation is strictly limited to the signed-in account owner. The requirements state that each profile is private to its owner, is available only within that member's own account context, and must not be browsed, searched, or opened across users. For that reason, this endpoint does not accept any profile identifier in the path and does not provide any mechanism to inspect another member's profile. When a person is not signed in, the request must be rejected and no profile details may be revealed.

This operation is backed by the one-to-one relationship between `todo_app_profiles` and `todo_app_members`, where `todo_app_profiles.todo_app_member_id` references the owning member account. The returned resource should expose the member's own profile information, centered on the `display_name` field and the profile record metadata represented by the DTO. Because the profile is created as part of account availability and associated with exactly one account owner, the endpoint should resolve a single profile for the authenticated member rather than perform any list or search behavior.

Clients typically use this operation when rendering account settings, profile summary views, or other private screens that need the current member's display name and profile details. No pre-execution of another profile API is required, because this endpoint is purpose-built to directly resolve the caller's own profile from authentication context. Error handling must prevent information leakage by returning only authorization-appropriate failures when the caller is unauthenticated or when no accessible profile can be served in the caller's own account scope.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated member from the request's authorization/session context. Do not accept or derive any alternate target member identifier from client input.

Query `todo_app_profiles` for the single row whose `todo_app_member_id` matches the authenticated member's `id`. Because the schema defines `@@unique([todo_app_member_id])`, expect at most one active profile row for a member. Return the profile as `ITodoAppProfile`.

Enforce member-only access. If the request is unauthenticated, reject the operation without exposing any profile details. If no profile can be resolved for the authenticated member, return a not-found or unavailable failure consistent with service conventions, but never expose information about any other member.

Do not implement browsing, search, or cross-user lookup behavior. Do not use path parameters. The service should only read the caller's own profile in their private account scope.

When mapping the response, include the profile fields defined by the DTO from the `todo_app_profiles` model, especially the private display name and record metadata. If the implementation distinguishes inactive records using `deleted_at`, it must ensure that only the caller's currently accessible profile is returned according to account lifecycle handling.

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated member's active todo list with filtering, sorting, and pagination.

This operation returns todo items from the private workspace owned by the authenticated member. It is the primary browsing endpoint for the member's active tasks and is intended for normal list views rather than trash management. In the todo application domain, a Todo is a personal private task owned by one user account, and all list results must remain limited to that same account.

Access is restricted to an authenticated member acting only within the account that was authenticated. The operation must never expose another member's todo items. It returns only todos that are still in normal active use and excludes items that have been moved to trash, because active-list browsing and trash browsing are separate user journeys in the requirements.

The request body supports structured list criteria such as pagination, filtering, and sorting. Completion-status filtering must support the business choices of all todos, only complete todos, and only incomplete todos. If the chosen criteria produce no matches, the operation still succeeds and returns an empty paginated list rather than treating the result as an error.

Sorting behavior must preserve a useful browsing experience for optional scheduling information. When the list is ordered by planned start timing or due timing, todos without those optional values should appear after todos that do have them so that undated items do not interrupt the ordered results.

This endpoint is commonly used before a member opens one todo for detail viewing or performs a separate update operation. Edit history is related to todo changes, but history entries are created automatically during edit flows and are not managed by this list endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement this operation as an authenticated member-only search over todo_app_todos for the caller's own active records.

Resolve the current member identity from the authentication context, and do not accept any member identifier from the request body. Build the query with a mandatory ownership predicate todo_app_member_id = authenticated member ID and a mandatory active-list predicate deleted_at IS NULL.

Apply pagination from ITodoAppTodo.IRequest using the project's standard paginated query pattern. Return a paginated result container of type IPageITodoAppTodo.ISummary. The summary projection should contain fields appropriate for list browsing from todo_app_todos, such as id, title, description preview if defined by DTO schema, start_date, due_date, completed, updated_at, and other summary-safe fields available in the DTO definition.

Apply completion-status filtering only when the request includes that criterion. Accept exactly the business values representing all todos, only complete todos, and only incomplete todos. Translate them as follows: all todos means no completed predicate beyond deleted_at IS NULL; only complete todos means completed = true; only incomplete todos means completed = false. Reject any other value as a validation error before running the query.

Support sorting for common list fields, especially start_date, due_date, and updated_at when those sorts are part of the request DTO. When ordering by start_date or due_date, place null values last so that todos without those optional dates appear at the end of the list as required. Use deterministic secondary ordering, such as updated_at descending and id ascending, to keep pagination stable when primary sort values are identical.

Return an empty page result when no records match the requested filters instead of treating that case as an error. Do not include trashed records in any branch of this operation. Do not create or modify TodoEditHistory here, because history entries are created only during todo edit operations and are never directly managed through list retrieval.

Use the existing indexes on todo_app_todos, especially the ownership and active-list indexes involving todo_app_member_id, deleted_at, updated_at, completed, and due_date, to keep member-scoped browsing efficient.

operations.description:
Create a new private todo item for the authenticated member.

This operation creates a record in the todo_app_todos table, which stores the core task data that members directly create and manage inside their personal todo workspace. The created todo belongs to exactly one member through the todo_app_member_id foreign key, and that ownership remains private to the authenticated account. The client supplies the task content fields that are user-managed at creation time: the required title and the optional description, start date, and due date. Server-managed lifecycle fields such as id, created_at, updated_at, and ownership are assigned by the system.

The created todo starts in the active list rather than the trash. In database terms, deleted_at is initialized as null so the item appears in the member's normal browsing flow, and the completion state starts as incomplete with completed set to false and completed_at left null. This matches the business journey in which a member first creates a todo and then later views it in their own active todo list, opens its full details, and may subsequently toggle completion or edit its content.

Access to this operation is restricted to the authenticated member actor. A member can create todos only within their own private workspace, and the system must never allow the caller to choose another member as the owner. The ownership boundary described in the requirements means that todo data is isolated per account, so this endpoint must derive the target owner from the authenticated session context and not from client-provided identifiers.

Validation should focus on the business attributes that are actually present on the todo record. The title is required because the schema defines it as a required task title shown in the member's private todo lists. Description is optional and may be omitted. Start date and due date are optional planned scheduling fields and may be omitted independently. The endpoint should reject malformed input that does not conform to the create DTO, while leaving edit-history concerns to later update operations.

This operation is commonly followed by browsing and detail retrieval APIs for the member's own todos. After creation succeeds, the returned resource can be shown immediately in the UI and later surfaced through the active todo list, which displays summary information such as title, completion status, creation date, and optional schedule dates. Edit history is not created by this operation because history entries are reserved for later edits to an existing todo.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Authenticate the caller as a member and resolve the owner member ID from the active session context.

Validate the request body against ITodoAppTodo.ICreate. Accept only the user-managed creation fields: title as required, and description, startDate, and dueDate as optional fields if those are defined by the DTO mapping for the todo entity. Do not accept ownership fields, completion lifecycle fields, trash lifecycle fields, or timestamp fields from the client.

Create a new todo_app_todos row with a freshly generated UUID id, todo_app_member_id set from the authenticated member, title and optional content fields mapped from the request, completed initialized to false, completed_at initialized to null, deleted_at initialized to null, and created_at and updated_at set to the current timestamp.

Return the created todo as ITodoAppTodo. The response should include persisted server-managed fields so the client can immediately render the new resource.

Do not create a todo edit history row during this operation. Requirement coverage states that TodoEditHistory entries are created automatically when an existing todo is edited, and direct history management is prohibited.

Handle authorization failure by rejecting unauthenticated access. Handle invalid input by rejecting requests that omit the required title or provide values that do not match the DTO schema. Use a single insert operation; no multi-step transaction is required unless surrounding infrastructure mandates transaction wrapping for consistency.

requestBody.description: Information required to create a todo

operations.description:
Retrieve the full details of one active todo owned by the authenticated member.

This operation returns a single private todo record from the member's personal todo workspace. It is intended for the use case where a member opens one of their own todos from the active todo list to inspect its complete information, including the optional longer description. The returned resource is based on the core task data stored in the todo_app_todos table, which contains the required task title shown in private todo lists, the optional longer task description, optional planned start date and due date, the completion flag, the completion timestamp, and the creation and update timestamps.

Access to this operation is restricted to the member who owns the todo. The todo_app_todos model defines each record as belonging to exactly one todo_app_members record through todo_app_member_id, and the requirements establish that todo browsing remains private so a user can view only their own todos and no other user's todos. The service must therefore resolve the authenticated member from the session context and verify that the requested todo belongs to that member before returning any data.

This endpoint is for active todos in the member's normal workspace view. The underlying schema uses deleted_at to indicate when a todo has been moved to trash, and the loaded browsing requirements state that the normal todo list shows only active todos and does not show deleted todos. For consistency with that active-list behavior, this operation should return the detail view only when deleted_at is null. A trashed todo, a todo owned by another member, or a nonexistent todo must not be exposed through this endpoint.

Clients typically reach this operation after first browsing the member's active todo list through the list endpoint for todos. That list provides summary information such as title, completion status, creation date, start date when present, and due date when present. This detail endpoint complements that browsing flow by returning the full todo object for the selected item, including fields needed for a detailed view or edit form.

If the identifier is malformed, the request should be rejected during parameter validation. If no matching active todo exists for the authenticated member, the service should return a not-found style error without revealing whether the underlying record exists for another member. This preserves the application's private ownership boundary while giving consistent behavior for missing or inaccessible records.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Implement a read-only service method that retrieves one row from todo_app_todos by id and authenticated ownership.

Resolve the authenticated member from the session or request context. Validate that the todoId path parameter is a UUID. Query todo_app_todos with a predicate equivalent to: id = :todoId AND todo_app_member_id = :memberId AND deleted_at IS NULL. Return exactly one record mapped to ITodoAppTodo when found.

Do not include records that have been moved to trash. The deleted_at column is the lifecycle marker for trashed items, and this active-detail endpoint must only expose rows where deleted_at is null. Do not join or mutate todo_app_todo_edit_histories here; history viewing is a separate concern and history records are created automatically only during edit operations.

If no row matches the predicate, return a not-found error. Use the same not-found behavior whether the todo does not exist, belongs to another member, or is in trash, so the implementation does not disclose ownership or hidden record state. No database transaction is required beyond the single read query. Ensure the response includes all persisted todo fields needed by the detailed DTO, including title, description, start_date, due_date, completed, completed_at, created_at, and updated_at.

responseBody.description: Detailed information for the requested todo

operations.description:
Update a specific todo that belongs to the authenticated member.

This operation modifies a private todo item stored in the todo_app_todos table, which is described as the core task data that members directly create, browse, update, complete, move to trash, restore, and permanently remove within their personal todo workspace. The target record is identified by the todo_app_todos.id primary key, and only the member who owns the todo through todo_app_todos.todo_app_member_id is allowed to update it. The editable business attributes align with the todo model and requirements: the required task title shown in the member's private todo lists, the optional longer description for additional details, the optional planned start date and time, the optional due date and time, and the completion state used for normal task tracking.

Security for this operation is strictly private and member-scoped. The application must confirm that the authenticated member is the owner of the target todo before applying any change. A member cannot update another member's todo, and the update must not cross ownership boundaries. Because the todo model separates active-list behavior from trash behavior through the deleted_at column, this operation is intended for an owned todo resource in the member's workspace and must reject update attempts when the target record is not available for normal editing under the product's deletion and browsing rules.

This operation is also linked to the todo_app_todo_edit_histories table, which stores chronological edit history records for a member-owned todo. Requirements state that the application automatically creates one new history entry as part of a todo edit and records the changed values when title, description, start date, or due date are modified. That historical child entity is system-managed rather than user-managed, so clients do not submit history data directly here and must use the separate history viewing operation to inspect the edit timeline. Completion changes remain part of normal todo management, while direct history creation, modification, and deletion are intentionally unavailable to members.

The response returns the updated todo resource so the client can immediately refresh the detail view after editing. This operation is commonly used after the member has opened a todo from their own active list. Related flows include listing owned active todos, opening a single todo detail, toggling completion status, and reviewing the todo's recorded edit history after a detail change has been saved. Error handling must cover nonexistent todos, access to another member's todo, and attempts to edit records that are no longer available in the normal active workspace.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target todo_app_todos row by id and authenticated member context.

Validate that a todo with the given id exists and that todo_app_member_id matches the authenticated member's id. If no matching owned row exists, return a not-found or access-denied failure according to the service's ownership-hiding policy. Also validate that the todo is still editable in the active workspace; if deleted_at is not null, reject the update because trashed todos are handled through trash-specific operations rather than normal edit flow.

Apply the request body to the editable columns only: title, description, start_date, due_date, and completed. Do not allow changes to id, todo_app_member_id, created_at, updated_at, or deleted_at from this operation. Update updated_at to the current timestamp on every successful modification.

For completion-state handling, synchronize completed and completed_at together. When completed changes from false to true, set completed_at to the current timestamp. When completed changes from true to false, clear completed_at to null. If completed is unchanged, preserve completed_at unless the service intentionally normalizes inconsistent legacy data.

Create one todo_app_todo_edit_histories row automatically when any of the detail fields tracked by history change: title, description, start_date, or due_date. Use a single history row per update request even if multiple tracked fields changed in the same request, and set created_at on the history row to the update event time. Do not create history rows for requests that only toggle completed without changing any tracked detail field, unless downstream domain rules explicitly require broader audit coverage.

Execute the todo update and any required history insert in a single transaction so the todo state and chronological edit record remain consistent. After commit, return the refreshed todo representation. Ensure the implementation supports repeated completion toggles safely and treats absent optional date fields as nullable values rather than invalid placeholders.

responseBody.description: Updated todo details

prerequisites.description: A member-owned todo must be created first so the update operation has a valid todoId for an existing active todo resource.

operations.description:
Permanently remove a member-owned todo that is already in trash.

This operation is for the private todo workspace used by an authenticated member to manage their own tasks. The underlying todo_app_todos model stores the core task data that members directly create, browse, update, complete, move to trash, restore, and permanently remove. This endpoint performs the final removal step for one specific todo after it has already been moved out of the active list into trash. It is not a general delete for active todos; it is the irreversible removal action for a trashed todo.

Access is limited to the authenticated member who owns the target todo. The todo_app_todos table records ownership through todo_app_member_id, and the service must ensure that one member cannot remove another member's private task. If the referenced todo does not belong to the current member, the operation must be denied as unavailable to that caller. This preserves the application's private access boundary for all todo and trash operations.

The todo's deleted state is represented by the deleted_at column. A null deleted_at value means the todo is still in the active list, while a non-null deleted_at value means the todo is in trash. The business rules require that permanent removal be allowed only for items currently in trash. Therefore, this endpoint must verify that the target record exists, belongs to the signed-in member, and has a non-null deleted_at value before deletion proceeds. If the todo is still active or has already been removed, the request must be rejected or treated as unavailable for permanent deletion.

This operation also affects the child history entity stored in todo_app_todo_edit_histories. That table contains chronological edit history records for a specific todo through todo_app_todo_id, and its lifecycle follows the parent todo. When a trashed todo is permanently removed, the associated edit history must no longer remain available. Because the relation from todo_app_todo_edit_histories to todo_app_todos is configured with cascade deletion, removing the parent todo will also remove its related history rows as part of the same outcome.

This endpoint is typically used after the member has already managed the todo through other todo APIs, such as listing active todos, moving a todo to trash, and browsing the trash list to choose an item for final removal. Once this operation succeeds, the todo is removed from trash and can no longer be restored or viewed through normal todo or trash browsing paths. Error handling must clearly distinguish invalid state, missing ownership, and unavailable targets without exposing another member's data.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implement a member-authenticated service operation that permanently deletes one todo_app_todos row by its id.

1. Resolve the authenticated member identity from the authorization context.
2. Load the target todo_app_todos record by id and owner together, using todo_app_todos.id = :todoId and todo_app_member_id = :currentMemberId.
3. If no row is found for that owner, return a not-found or unavailable error without revealing whether the id belongs to another member.
4. Validate deletion state by checking deleted_at. If deleted_at is null, reject the request because permanent deletion is allowed only for todos already in trash.
5. Delete the todo_app_todos row inside a transaction. The related todo_app_todo_edit_histories rows should be removed automatically by the existing foreign-key cascade on todo_app_todo_id.
6. Commit the transaction and return success with no response body.

Implementation must not create any direct API-level behavior for deleting individual history rows, because history lifecycle is managed only through parent todo removal. The operation should be idempotent only to the extent required by unavailable-target handling: if the todo has already been permanently removed, subsequent requests should be treated as not found or unavailable rather than recreating any state.

Do not allow permanent deletion of active todos. Active-item removal must first occur through the separate trashing workflow that sets deleted_at. Ensure all queries are scoped by the authenticated member to preserve private data isolation.

prerequisites.description: The target todo must exist before it can be permanently removed from trash; this operation creates the member-owned todo identified later by todoId.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of the authenticated member's todo items that are currently in trash.

This operation is the dedicated browsing entry point for deleted todos within the private todo workspace. It returns only todo records that belong to the requesting member and that have already been moved out of the active list into trash. In the underlying todo_app_todos table, this trash membership is represented by the deleted_at column being populated, while the todo remains the same business item with its original title, optional description, optional start_date, optional due_date, completion flag, and lifecycle timestamps preserved until permanent removal. The response is intended for trash list screens and similar list-oriented user interfaces, so it should provide summary-oriented todo information together with pagination metadata.

Access to this operation is restricted to the authenticated member actor. The todo_app_todos model is explicitly private to its owner through the todo_app_member_id foreign key, and the service must always derive that ownership scope from the authenticated session instead of accepting ownership criteria from client input. This privacy boundary is mandatory for both non-empty and empty pages. Even when the requested page is beyond the available result set, the response must still reflect only the requesting member's own deleted todos and must never reveal or infer data from another member's workspace.

The operation supports trash browsing behavior described in the requirements for deleted-state handling. Deleted todos must not appear in the normal todo list, and this endpoint must do the inverse by returning only deleted todos. Filtering and sorting are applied after the mandatory ownership and deleted-state constraints have been enforced. When sorting by start date or due date, records with null start_date or null due_date must be placed at the end of the ordered results. If completion-status filtering is supported through the request DTO, it applies only within the member's deleted todos rather than mixing active and deleted records.

This endpoint is commonly used together with other todo lifecycle operations. A member would typically browse the active list through the normal todo index, move a todo into trash through the delete operation, then use this trash index to find items eligible for restoration or permanent removal. After a successful restore operation, the restored todo should no longer be returned by this endpoint because it is no longer in the deleted state. After a successful permanent removal operation, the todo and its related edit history are no longer available and therefore cannot appear in subsequent trash results.

If the member requests a page beyond the available trash results, the service must return an empty data set for that page instead of raising an error solely because the page is empty. Error handling should focus on authentication and access context, malformed request-body search or sort input, and internal lookup or query failures. The endpoint should treat deleted-state membership as a strict inclusion rule for this list and must not return active todos under any filter or sort combination.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement a member-scoped trash browsing query over todo_app_todos.

Authenticate the caller as a member and obtain the member identifier from the authenticated session context. Build the base query with a mandatory WHERE clause requiring todo_app_member_id to equal the authenticated member ID and deleted_at to be non-null. Do not allow the client request body to override either ownership scope or trash-state scope.

Accept an ITodoAppTodo.IRequest body for pagination, filtering, and sorting input. Apply supported filters only within the already constrained deleted todo dataset. If completion-status filtering is provided, map it to the completed column. If text search is supported by the DTO, restrict it to fields that actually exist in todo_app_todos, such as title and optionally description, using implementation-appropriate matching. Do not reference non-existent status columns or imagined ownership fields.

Implement sorting using the real schema columns. Support creation-date ordering via created_at. Support start-date ordering via start_date and due-date ordering via due_date. For start_date and due_date sorts, ensure null values are ordered last regardless of ascending or descending direction, matching the browsing requirements for undated todos. Apply a deterministic secondary sort such as updated_at DESC or id ASC as needed to avoid unstable pagination when primary sort values are duplicated.

Return paginated summary results as IPageITodoAppTodo.ISummary. The summary projection should be sufficient for trash list presentation and should include fields aligned with the requirements for list browsing, such as title, completed, created_at, start_date, due_date, and deleted_at when the DTO definition supports it. Avoid returning unrelated child history data from this list operation.

If the requested page is beyond the available rows, return an empty page result rather than an error. Preserve the member scope for empty-page responses exactly as for populated responses. Validate request-body values according to DTO rules and reject malformed sort/filter combinations. Keep this operation read-only: it must not restore, permanently remove, or otherwise mutate any todo row. Those state transitions belong to separate operations.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of deleted todo summaries in trash

requestBody.description: Trash list search, filter, sort, and pagination options

operations.description:
Restore a deleted todo from trash back to the member's active todo list.

This operation allows an authenticated member to recover one of their own private todo items after it has been moved to trash. In the underlying todo_app_todos model, a todo remains the same record throughout its lifecycle and the trash state is represented by the deleted_at column. Restoring the todo clears that deleted-state marker so the item is no longer treated as a trash entry and appears again in the member's normal todo list. The restored todo keeps its original task data, including the required title, optional description, optional start date, optional due date, completion flag, completion timestamp, creation timestamp, and update timestamp.

Access to this operation is restricted to the authenticated member who owns the todo through todo_app_member_id. A member must never be able to restore another member's todo. If the specified todo does not belong to the requesting member, the request must be rejected as unavailable or forbidden according to the service's error policy. This preserves the application's private ownership boundary in which each member manages only their own profile and todos.

The operation is specifically for todos that are currently in trash. Business rules require deleted todos to be excluded from the normal list and shown only in the trash context while deleted_at is set. If a member attempts to restore a todo that is not currently deleted, the request must be rejected because the restore action is only valid for a todo already in the deleted state. On success, the todo returns to the active list rather than creating a new replacement record.

This restore behavior also preserves the relationship between todo_app_todos and todo_app_todo_edit_histories. The todo's edit history remains associated with the same todo after recovery and continues to be available as part of that todo's lifecycle. Direct creation, modification, or deletion of history entries is not exposed by the API, so this endpoint changes only the todo's deleted-state marker and active-list availability.

This endpoint is typically used after the member has already browsed deleted items through the trash-list operation and selected a specific todo to recover. After this operation succeeds, normal todo-list and todo-detail operations should treat the restored item as active again, while trash-oriented operations should no longer include it.
operations.name: restore
operations.specification:
Implement a service action that restores a member-owned todo from trash by clearing the deleted-state marker on todo_app_todos.

Authenticate the caller as a member and resolve the target todo by todo_app_todos.id using the todoId path parameter together with the caller's member identifier. The lookup must enforce ownership by filtering on both id and todo_app_member_id so that one member cannot restore another member's todo.

Validate that the located todo currently has a non-null deleted_at value. If no owned todo is found, return the service's not-found or forbidden outcome for inaccessible resources. If the todo exists but deleted_at is already null, reject the request as an invalid restore attempt because the todo is not in trash.

On success, update the row in a single write operation by setting deleted_at to null and updating updated_at to the current timestamp. Do not modify title, description, start_date, due_date, completed, completed_at, or created_at as part of restoration. Do not create a new todo record.

Do not alter related todo_app_todo_edit_histories during restore. History rows remain attached to the same todo and continue to exist after the todo returns to the active list. No manual history entry should be created solely for this restore action unless a separate cross-cutting audit mechanism exists outside this domain model.

Return the refreshed todo entity after the update. The response mapping should reflect the restored active state, including deleted_at as null. Ensure subsequent active-list queries include this todo again and trash-list queries exclude it after restoration.

Handle concurrent or repeated restore requests safely. If the first request succeeds and a later request targets the same todo after it is already active, the later request must be rejected because the todo is no longer in the deleted state.

responseBody.description: The restored todo item

prerequisites.description: The target todo must already exist as a member-owned todo record before it can be restored from trash using its todoId.

operations.description:
Retrieve the edit history entries for a single todo that belongs to the authenticated member.

This operation provides the full TodoEditHistory view for one member-owned todo inside the private todo workspace. The history entity represents the chronological record of edits made to a todo, and each entry is presented with its recorded edit time. When a history entry captured changes to editable values such as title, description, start date, or due date, the response should expose only the values that were actually recorded for that edit event.

Access is limited to the authenticated member who owns the target todo. Before returning any history data, the service must verify that the referenced todo exists and is owned by the current member account. Todo history is private account data, so a signed-out caller must be rejected and a caller must never be allowed to view history for another member's todo.

The result is intended for history review after a member has created and later revised a todo. Entries must be presented from most recent to oldest so the caller can inspect the latest changes first. If the todo has never been edited after creation, the operation should return an empty paginated result and must not fabricate change records or imply that unchanged values were edited.

This operation is part of the broader todo maintenance flow. A client will commonly retrieve or inspect the parent todo first, then call this endpoint to review the sequence of past edits for that same todo. History remains available while the related todo exists, including when the todo is in trash, and becomes unavailable after the todo has been permanently removed.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
1. Require authenticated member context.
2. Resolve the parent todo by todo_app_todos.id = :todoId.
3. If no todo exists for the supplied identifier, return a not-found error.
4. Compare todo_app_todos.todo_app_member_id with the authenticated member identifier. If they do not match, reject the request as access denied.
5. If the parent todo has been permanently removed, treat the history as unavailable through the same not-found path because the parent row and child history rows no longer exist.
6. Parse ITodoAppTodoEditHistory.IRequest for pagination and optional retrieval controls. Do not require the client to send todoId in the request body because the parent context is already supplied by the path.
7. Query todo_app_todo_edit_histories filtered by todo_app_todo_id = :todoId.
8. Order results by created_at descending so the newest edit entry is returned first, matching the business rule for history review.
9. Return a paginated IPageITodoAppTodoEditHistory.ISummary payload. If there are no matching rows, return an empty page successfully.
10. Map each history row into the summary DTO using only persisted history fields and any DTO properties derived from the history record. Do not infer edits that were not recorded.
11. This operation is read-only. Do not create, update, or delete history rows here. History creation occurs automatically during todo update workflows, and history deletion occurs only when the parent todo is permanently removed from trash.
12. Prefer an index-assisted query using the existing @@index([todo_app_todo_id, created_at]) on todo_app_todo_edit_histories to support efficient newest-first retrieval.

responseBody.description: Paginated edit history entries for the specified owned todo

parameters.description: Target todo's ID owned by the authenticated member
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: Pagination and retrieval options for one owned todo's edit history

prerequisites.description: A member-owned todo must exist before its edit history can be retrieved, because the target operation resolves the parent todo by todoId and lists history rows only for that existing todo.

operations.description:
Retrieve one recorded edit-history entry for a specific todo owned by the authenticated member.

This operation returns the detail view of a single TodoEditHistory entry that belongs to the specified todo. In the underlying data model, `todo_app_todo_edit_histories` is the chronological edit-history child table for `todo_app_todos`, and each row captures one recorded edit event for a specific parent todo through `todo_app_todo_id`. The history entry is not an independent user-managed object; it exists only as part of the todo's own business record and is presented in the context of that parent todo.

Access to this operation is private to the owning member. The service must verify that the target todo belongs to the authenticated member using the ownership boundary defined by `todo_app_todos.todo_app_member_id`, and must also verify that the requested history entry is attached to that same todo. The system must deny access when the todo belongs to another member, when the caller is not authenticated, or when the todo and its history are no longer available because the parent todo was permanently removed.

The response represents one historical edit event, including the recorded edit time derived from `todo_app_todo_edit_histories.created_at` and the changed values stored for that edit when present. According to the business requirements, a history entry may include changed title, description, start date, and due date values, and it must not imply that unchanged values were edited. This operation therefore complements the full history-list view for a todo by allowing a client to access a particular entry directly when its identifier is already known from the parent history listing.

Clients typically obtain available history entry identifiers from the history listing of the same todo before calling this detail endpoint. The parent todo context in the path is required because the history is conceptually attached to one todo only, and that scoping helps enforce both privacy and relational integrity. Error handling should avoid disclosing whether another member's todo exists beyond the access rules required by the private workspace model.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Implement this operation as a member-authenticated read on the nested todo history resource.

1. Authenticate the caller as a member. Reject unauthenticated requests.
2. Resolve the parent todo by `todoId` from `todo_app_todos`. The lookup must enforce ownership by requiring `id = :todoId` and `todo_app_member_id = currentMemberId`.
3. If no owned todo matches, return the service's not-found or access-denied result according to project conventions, without exposing another member's private data.
4. Query `todo_app_todo_edit_histories` for the requested `editHistoryId` with `id = :editHistoryId` and `todo_app_todo_id = :todoId`. This guarantees the history entry belongs to the specified parent todo.
5. If no matching history row exists, return not found.
6. Map the record to `ITodoAppTodoEditHistory`. Populate the edit timestamp from `created_at`. Include the changed title, description, start date, and due date values only when that edit entry actually recorded them in the domain DTO representation; do not fabricate unchanged fields.
7. Return the single mapped DTO.

Implementation notes:
- No transaction is required because this is a read-only operation.
- Do not provide any mutation behavior for history entries here.
- Preserve the nested-resource invariant: even if a history ID exists, it must not be returned unless it is attached to the specified owned todo.
- If the parent todo has already been permanently removed, the history should be treated as unavailable because cascade deletion removes child history rows with the parent.
- Logging and auditing, if implemented, should avoid leaking private todo content in application logs.

authorizations.name: member
authorizations.description: Authenticated user who registers with email and password, manages their own profile, creates and manages their own todos, views edit history, uses trash, and can delete their account.

current.description:
Current page number being viewed (1-indexed).

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Actual count may be less on last page.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is
essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render
page navigation controls and validate page bounds.
pages.x-autobe-specification: Total pages. Calculated as Math.ceil(records / limit).

IPage.IPagination.description:
Pagination metadata containing current page position and total data
statistics.

This interface provides comprehensive pagination information returned
alongside paginated list data. It enables clients to implement navigation
controls, display progress indicators, and determine data boundaries for UI
rendering.
IPage.IPagination.x-autobe-specification: Pagination metadata for paginated list responses. Included in all list endpoint responses.

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the todo item was moved to trash, or null if it is currently active.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_todos.deleted_at. Return the timestamp when the todo was moved to trash, or null when the todo is active.

ITodoAppTodo.description: Complete todo resource for the authenticated member's private workspace. This schema represents one persisted todo item with its task content, optional scheduling data, completion state, and lifecycle timestamps as returned by todo creation, detail retrieval, update, and restore APIs.
ITodoAppTodo.x-autobe-specification: Direct read-model mapping from todo_app_todos for a single member-owned todo entity returned by create, detail, update, and restore operations. Populate id, title, description, start_date, due_date, completed, completed_at, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at directly from the row selected or mutated in todo_app_todos. Preserve nullable response values for description, start_date, due_date, completed_at, and deleted_at exactly as stored in the database. Do not expose todo_app_member_id because ownership is enforced from authenticated session context rather than returned in this DTO. Do not inline member or edit-history relations in this schema; member ownership and edit history are handled by authorization logic and separate endpoints respectively.

search.description: Optional keyword used to narrow the signed-in member's email verification history.
search.x-autobe-specification: Optional free-text filter for narrowing the authenticated member's own email verification history. Apply it as a token-oriented search against todo_app_member_email_verifications records already constrained by todo_app_member_id from the session context. When omitted, do not add search filtering.

state.description: Optional lifecycle state filter for showing active, used, revoked, or expired verification records.
state.x-autobe-specification: Optional lifecycle-state selector for member-scoped verification browsing. Translate active to expired_at > now with used_at and revoked_at both null; used to used_at IS NOT NULL; revoked to revoked_at IS NOT NULL; expired to expired_at <= now with used_at and revoked_at both null; null means no lifecycle-state filtering. Apply deleted_at handling separately through includeDeleted.

includeDeleted.description: Whether soft-deleted email verification records should be included in the search results.
includeDeleted.x-autobe-specification: Optional boolean controlling whether soft-deleted todo_app_member_email_verifications rows with deleted_at set may appear in the result set. When true, allow deleted rows to participate alongside other filters. When false or omitted, exclude rows where deleted_at is non-null.

sort.description: Optional sort order for the email verification records returned by the list operation.
sort.x-autobe-specification: Optional deterministic ordering selector for the member-scoped verification query. Support the enumerated timestamp orderings exactly as defined by the schema: created_at_desc, created_at_asc, updated_at_desc, updated_at_asc, expired_at_desc, expired_at_asc. When omitted, default to created_at descending.

page.description: Optional page number to return from the filtered email verification results.
page.x-autobe-specification: Optional 1-indexed page number for paginating the filtered verification result set. Apply after authentication scope, filtering, and ordering. When omitted, default to the first page.

limit.description: Optional maximum number of email verification records to include in one page of results.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Optional maximum number of records to return per page for the member-scoped verification query. Enforce the schema bounds of minimum 1 and maximum 100. When omitted, use the operation's default page size.

ITodoAppMemberEmailVerification.IRequest.description: Filtering, sorting, and pagination criteria for browsing the signed-in member's email verification records. This request body lets a member narrow their own verification history by keyword, lifecycle state, deleted-record visibility, ordering, and page controls without supplying account identity in the payload.
ITodoAppMemberEmailVerification.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: This schema defines structured request criteria for the member-scoped PATCH /todoApp/member/emailVerifications list operation. Implement it as a non-persisted query DTO that controls filtering, lifecycle-state interpretation, sorting, and pagination for reads against todo_app_member_email_verifications. Always derive account scope from the authenticated member session and apply todo_app_member_id = authenticated member id in the operation layer; never accept member identity or any other account scope from this body. Interpret search as an optional token-oriented text filter over the member's own verification records. Interpret state as a business lifecycle selector translated into predicates over expired_at, used_at, revoked_at, deleted_at, and current server time: active means expired_at is in the future with used_at and revoked_at both null; used means used_at is non-null; revoked means revoked_at is non-null; expired means expired_at is in the past while used_at and revoked_at are null. Interpret includeDeleted as a switch controlling whether rows with deleted_at set may participate in the result set. Interpret sort as deterministic ordering over the supported timestamp fields, defaulting to newest created_at first when omitted. Interpret page and limit as pagination controls applied after filtering and ordering. This DTO does not map to a single database table row and must not be used for create, update, or direct persistence.

The API interface is already up to date, so the prerequisite for E2E test generation is satisfied.

I’m now generating the end-to-end test functions for the multi-user todo application API.

scenario.draft: Test the primary member registration workflow where a new person submits a unique email address together with a password and the required session-context fields href and referrer, optionally including ip. Verify that the public sign-up request succeeds, creates a new private member account, and immediately returns an authorized member response without requiring a separate login. Validate that the response contains the new member id, normalized email identity, email_verified state, created_at and updated_at timestamps, deleted_at as null for an active account, and a token bundle with access token, refresh token, access expiration, and refreshable-until metadata. Confirm the issued authorization represents the newly created member's own private account context.

dependencies.purpose:
Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /todoApp/auth/member/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'member' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'member' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

functions.name: test_api_member_join_success

scenario.draft: Test the duplicate-registration business rule using this single endpoint as a two-step scenario. First, submit a registration request with a unique email and confirm the account is created successfully with an authorized response. Then submit another registration request to the same endpoint using the same email identity and a different password for a new attempted account. Verify that the second request is rejected because an active account with that email already exists, and confirm the rejection does not create a second private ownership root or replace the original active account.

functions.name: test_api_member_join_duplicate_email_rejected

scenario.draft: Test email normalization during registration as a duplicate-prevention rule within the join flow. First, register a member using an email address in one letter-case form and confirm success. Next, call the same registration endpoint again using the same logical email in a different casing. Verify that the second request is rejected because the system normalizes email identity consistently for uniqueness checks, preventing creation of multiple member accounts that differ only by casing.

functions.name: test_api_member_join_email_normalization_duplicate_rejected

scenario.draft: Register a new member first through the member join endpoint, then call login with the same email and password. Verify that login succeeds for the existing active account, returns the authorized member payload with the member identity fields and a token bundle, and does not expose password storage details. Validate that the response includes a non-empty access token, non-empty refresh token, an access expiration timestamp, and a refreshable-until timestamp, and that the returned member email matches the registered account. This scenario confirms the core business rule that a member can sign in after successful registration using the same credential pair and receive a fresh authenticated session.

dependencies.purpose: Create a real member account whose credentials can be used for the login attempt.

functions.name: test_api_member_login_success

scenario.draft: Register a member account, then attempt login with the correct email but a different password value than the one used at registration. Verify that the login request is rejected as a credential-pair mismatch and that the failure does not disclose whether the email or password was the incorrect part of the pair. Confirm that no authorized member payload or usable access and refresh tokens are returned. This scenario validates the business rule that the system evaluates email and password as one account credential pair and rejects sign-in when they do not match the same existing active account.

dependencies.purpose: Create an existing active member so the test can exercise a wrong-password credential-pair rejection against a real account.

functions.name: test_api_member_login_credential_pair_rejected

scenario.draft: Attempt login with a credential pair that does not correspond to any active member account, covering either a never-registered email address or credentials for an account that is no longer active because it is deleted. Verify that the login request is rejected and that the response does not reveal whether the failure was caused by account absence, deletion state, or password mismatch. Confirm that no authorization tokens are issued. This scenario validates the business rule that only active existing accounts can authenticate and that deleted or unavailable accounts must not be allowed to sign in.
