scenario.draft: Verify that a member who already has an authorized session from registration can renew authorization through the refresh endpoint. First create a new member account through the join endpoint and capture the issued token bundle, especially the refresh token. Then call the refresh endpoint with that refresh credential and confirm the response returns the same member account identity and email while issuing a fresh authorization token bundle for the same private account scope. Validate that the response includes a new access token, a refresh token, and updated expiration metadata, and that the operation renews authorization through the existing session lifecycle rather than creating access to any different account.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new authenticated member session and obtain the initial refresh credential used for renewal.

functions.name: test_api_member_refresh_after_join

scenario.draft: Verify that the refresh endpoint rejects a credential that does not belong to any valid current session context. Create one member account through the join endpoint to establish a normal authenticated baseline, then call the refresh endpoint with a malformed, revoked, mismatched, or otherwise non-resolvable refresh credential instead of the issued one. Confirm the request is rejected and no new authorized member context is returned. This scenario should prove the endpoint does not silently create a session, does not authenticate against a non-existent session row, and preserves the rule that refresh only works for an existing valid session tied to a real member account.

dependencies.purpose: Create a normal member account so the test can compare valid issued credentials against an unrelated or unusable refresh credential.

functions.name: test_api_member_refresh_session_not_found

scenario.draft: Verify that refresh is denied once the underlying session is no longer refreshable because the stored session expiration boundary has passed. Create a member account through the join endpoint, capture the issued refresh token and its refreshable lifetime metadata, then attempt refresh only after the session has expired according to the token and session lifecycle. Confirm the endpoint rejects the request instead of extending an expired session, and that no renewed authorization payload is returned. This scenario should validate the business rule that refresh depends on an existing non-expired session linked to an active member account.

dependencies.purpose: Create the member account and obtain the initial refresh credential whose usable lifetime will later expire.

functions.name: test_api_member_refresh_after_session_expired

scenario.draft: Register a new member account, then call this endpoint as that same signed-in member to retrieve the authenticated account summary in paginated form. Verify the result contains exactly the caller's own account record, that the returned summary matches the registered email identity, that pagination metadata is still present and consistent for a single-record page, and that only safe account fields are exposed in the summary response. Confirm the endpoint behaves as a private self-account lookup rather than a member directory and does not expose credential material such as any password hash.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate the member account whose own account record will be retrieved

functions.name: test_api_member_account_self_search

scenario.draft: Create and authenticate a member account, then call this endpoint within that authenticated session using valid filter combinations that attempt to narrow results in ways that would only matter if broader account visibility existed. Verify the query remains strictly scoped to the authenticated member's own account context, so the response can only contain the caller's own member summary when the filters match that account, or an empty page when the filters exclude the caller. Confirm that request filters refine results only within the caller's private scope and can never widen visibility to any other member account.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate the member whose private account scope is used for the query

functions.name: test_api_member_account_filter_scope_is_private

scenario.draft: Call this endpoint without any authenticated member session. Verify the request is rejected before any query logic runs, no account summaries or pagination data for a private account are disclosed, and the response does not reveal whether any particular email exists in the system. This confirms that account retrieval is available only to an authenticated member and that failed access does not leak private account information.

functions.name: test_api_member_account_access_denied_when_signed_out

scenario.draft: Authenticate as a newly registered member, then retrieve that same member account by using the authenticated member's own account identifier in the path. Verify the request succeeds only within the caller's own private account context and returns the safe member account representation for that owner. Confirm the response includes the expected account fields such as id, email, email_verified, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at, and that the returned id matches the authenticated member's account. Also verify that sensitive credential material is never exposed in the response, especially that password data is not returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate a member so the request runs inside that member's private account context

functions.name: test_api_member_account_self_retrieval

scenario.draft: Register and authenticate one member as the active caller, then within the scenario create a separate second member account to obtain a different member identifier. While still acting as the first member, request GET /todoApp/members/{memberId} using the second member's id. Verify the request is denied because member account access is strictly self-only, that no account details for the other member are disclosed, and that the private account boundary is preserved without exposing profile, todo, or other owned data of the target member.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate the first member who will attempt the self-only account lookup

functions.name: test_api_member_account_other_member_denied

scenario.draft: Authenticate as a new member through the member join endpoint, then update the signed-in member's own profile with a different display name. Verify the response returns the same profile identity and owning member summary while the displayName changes to the newly submitted value. Confirm the operation behaves as a private account-owner action by updating only the caller-resolved profile, preserving created_at and ownership linkage, and reflecting a refreshed updated_at for the changed profile record.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a member and create the private account context that owns exactly one profile.

functions.name: test_api_profile_update_own_display_name

scenario.draft: Authenticate as a new member and perform a profile update using the same display name already stored on that member's profile. Verify the endpoint returns the current profile representation without implying a substantive modification, leaves the profile data unchanged, and does not alter ownership-related fields. This scenario should focus on the business rule that repeated no-change updates are accepted as an idempotent outcome rather than treated as a meaningful profile change.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a member and create the private account context whose single profile will be updated.

functions.name: test_api_profile_update_same_display_name_no_change

scenario.draft: Call the profile update endpoint without any authenticated member session. Verify the request is rejected for signed-out users and that no profile update is performed. The test should confirm profile editing is available only within the caller's own authenticated account context and cannot be executed while signed out.

authorizations.error_analysis: The reported TypeScript compilation error is in src/MyGlobal.ts: TS2307 Cannot find module './MyConfiguration'. Although the authorization components themselves do not show direct type errors, the generated provider imports MyGlobal from ../../MyGlobal, which causes the authorization build path to fail transitively because MyGlobal.ts cannot compile. This means the provider cannot be type-checked successfully even if its own logic is otherwise valid. There are no naming convention issues: memberAuthorize, MemberAuth, and MemberPayload already match the required conventions.
authorizations.solution_guidance: To resolve the authorization compilation failure without weakening security, avoid importing the broken ../../MyGlobal module from the provider until that module's missing './MyConfiguration' dependency is restored. Replace the provider's database access dependency with a runtime-safe global Prisma access pattern via globalThis so the authorization component can compile independently of MyGlobal.ts. Keep JWT verification, payload.type role validation, member existence validation, deleted_at soft-delete filtering, and session expiration validation intact. The decorator and payload remain structurally correct, so no security logic should be removed or bypassed.
